text:
sam: Heads-up — ran into a repeatable SLA regression when prefetching KV for tiny requests. Pattern: prefetch fires, fills KV cache, but ends up delaying real-time small requests that had strict deadlines.

mica: can you paste a minimal repro or the request shape? sounds similar to the cold->hot warmup problem we saw last quarter. :thinking_face:

sam: repro: 95% requests are <= 32 tokens, 1% are long (>=1024). prefetch pipeline spawns background load for long ones with high batch size, it hoards GPU cycles and KV fetch bandwidth. short requests' latency p95 jumps ~40ms.

alex: ouch. are background prefetches running in same admission pool/priority? if so they should be soft-deprioritized.

sam: today they run in same lane with a prefetch_budget counter, but budget is global and refilled aggressively. when a tenant has a burst of long requests, budget drains and then refills, causing oscillation.

jordan: i think the root mismatch is contract: prefetch expects "best-effort" but admission treats it as "work to schedule" with equal weight. we need explicit semantics: prefetch=speculative, cannot bump deadline-sensitive tokens.

pat: what about propagating a deadline hint from API layer that marks low-priority prefetches? e.g., header X-Deadline-Hint or priority=speculative.

sam: exactly. proposal: 1) add X-Eligibility: speculative|regular header from admission; 2) scheduler maintains two separate micro-queues per lane: speculative queue (strictly capped) and regular queue; 3) telemetry: per-tenant metric prefetch_speculative_inflight and speculative_evict_count.

alex: two micro-queues sounds okay but we need to avoid head-of-line blocking when speculative queue is non-empty. suggest speculative only scheduled to spare slots after regular queue drained for current window.

mica: also need a soft cap not a hard one. hard cap could starve long but necessary work (e.g., batch warmups). soft cap with exponential backoff works: speculative gets scheduled up to soft_cap, beyond that it uses token-bucket with reduced refill rate.

jordan: agree. and include fast-fail path: if speculative prefetch can't get scheduled within prefetch_timeout (configurable per-tenant), it should abort — avoid indefinite resource holding. add metric speculative_abort_count.

sam: sample config snippet i ran locally:

```
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  soft_cap_per_lane: 8
  hard_cap_per_lane: 32
  refill_rate: 1/s
  speculative_timeout_ms: 120
```

pat: nice. what about rollout? we need feature flag per-cluster and per-tenant override. also add a canary that measures p95_small_requests before/after.

alex: telemetry gap: we currently only emit total_inflight and total_latency. add gauges: regular_inflight, speculative_inflight, speculative_queue_latency, speculative_to_regular_promotions. those will make it possible to detect misbehavior quickly.

mica: also ensure KV-cache warmup has explicit budget: warmup_prefetch_kv_bytes and warmup_prefetch_concurrency. otherwise you get cache thrash.

sam: followups: i'll open an RFC PR with the two-queue scheduler sketch, config knobs, and telemetry list. can we get +1 on the timeout + soft_cap idea?

jordan: +1 to soft cap + timeout. prefer token-bucket refill rate tweak over hard cap for safety.

pat: +1 and add a script in dev infra to replay small-request workload for canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flagged prefetch-queue-experiment scheduled to canary tonight at 02:00 UTC.

sam: thanks — i'll attach the RFC link and a small repro harness in the thread. :thumbsup:
